subdomain: 6.3 Manage stakeholder feedback loops and expectation alignment (including SLAs)

en.question: A parts-identification assistant's dashboard reports 99.9% success because its indicator counts HTTP 200 responses from the model gateway. Workshops report empty final results when a later inventory lookup fails. The agreed user journey ends only when a usable parts list is displayed. The product owner wants to preserve the existing reports for audit and resolve the discrepancy before expanding usage. What is the best next action?

options.text: Tighten the gateway's HTTP success target and retain its current measurement boundary so the existing audit series remains directly comparable.
options.note: A stricter target on the same incomplete boundary still cannot detect the downstream lookup failures users experience.

options.text: Increase the model's response budget and ask workshops to retry empty results, using reduced complaint volume as evidence the agreement is being met.
options.note: Neither change establishes whether downstream failures are measured or whether users receive the agreed usable result.

options.text: Correlate complaints with the complete request path, add a usable-result indicator, and obtain approval for a versioned measurement change while preserving history.
options.note: This tests the known coverage gap and aligns measurement with the agreed journey without rewriting historical evidence.

options.text: Reclassify inventory failures as external to the service and close the discrepancy because the component represented on the dashboard is healthy.
options.note: The agreed service boundary includes the displayed parts list, so excluding the inventory dependency contradicts the user-facing commitment.
